notes.title: Known Oculus Touch Issue - Patch Coming Soon
notes.content:

We're in the process of resolving that issue and will release a patch as soon as a fix is in place.

Thanks for your patience! 

~The Nevermind Team

notes.title: Build Notes for Version 1.52.10
notes.content:
[h1]Build Notes for Version 1.52.10 [/h1]

[h1]Updates:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b][u]Minor Improvements:[/u] Oculus Touch integration[/b]
We have made a few slight adjustments to Nevermind’s Oculus Touch integration for an even more responsive experience. 
 
[*][b][u]Minor Bug Fixes:[/u] Misc[/b]
Several miscellaneous bug fixes have been made.
[/list]


[h1]Ongoing Notes and Disclaimers:[/h1]
[list]
[*][b][u]Performance:[/u] Adjusting as Needed[/b] 
Due to a recent engine upgrade, Nevermind may run more smoothly on some machines, while it may hitch a bit more on others. If you notice decreased performance, [b]please consider lowering the screen resolution under Options>Graphics.[/b] 

[*][b][u]Vive:[/u] Known Issues[/b] 
There are a couple of known issues with playing Nevermind on the Vive. 

1.) During some scene loads, the game will fade away and the standard SteamVR "VR Room" will briefly appear.

2.) If you launch the game with both controllers on and then turn a controller off mid-game, you may experience odd behavior when interacting with an object. If this occurs, either turn the second controller back on and continue playing with it on OR quit the game and restart it with only one controller on. 

[*][b][u]Camera-Based Technology:[/u] Optimal Conditions[/b] 
Camera-based technology such as Affdex or RealSense can be influenced by environmental conditions such as lighting, location relative to the player, and objects in the background. If your camera-based technology hasn’t initialized after a few minutes into the game, please try the following:

>>>Double-check to ensure sure your camera technology has a good, centered view of your face.  Once the technology has initialized, you can refine your positioning further in the Options>Input screen. 

>>>Adjust the lighting in your room. Medium-strength overhead lights tend to work well. Lighting originating from the same height as your face (such as from a desk lamp) can sometimes prove to be problematic - especially if it is reflecting off of something like glasses or if a strong light falls on only one side of your face. 

>>>Ensure there are no other infrared emitting devices in close proximity of the camera technology and that reflective surfaces in the background are minimized. 

[*][b][u]Device Cross-Compatibility:[/u][/b]
Many of our devices are compatible with each other. However, some devices are mutually exclusive. Please visit www.nevermindgame.com/tech for the most up-to-date list of device cross-compatibility/incompatibility details. 

[*][b][u]Windows 7 Support:[/u][/b] 
[i]Nevermind[/i] is playable on [b]Windows 7[/b], although it is not fully supported. Windows 7 users may experience some instability.

[*][b][u]Mio LINK Users:[/u][/b] 
[b][u]Mio Link Bluetooth[/u][/b] connectivity works [b]only on Windows 8, 8.1, and 10[/b]. To pair a Mio LINK with a Windows 7 machine, please use an [url=smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00CM381SQ/ref=smi_www_rco2_go_smi_2096965542?ie=UTF8&camp=1789&creative=9325&creativeASIN=B00CM381SQ&linkCode=as2&linkId=X5Y3O2YXD6TU3SGD%2F&redirect=true&tag=nevermind0b-20] ANT+ USB [/url] stick. 

[*][b][u]Companion App:[/u][/b] 
To support non-RealSense heart rate devices (e.g. The Mio, Garmin Chest Strap, etc.) on Windows 7, 8, 8.1, & 10 environments, [i]Nevermind[/i] makes use of a small [b]companion app[/b] called the [i]Nevermind Heartrate Companion[/i]. This companion application is opened and closed by the game, and can be found as a taskbar icon next to the clock during play. This companion application uses network protocols to communicate with [i]Nevermind[/i]. Because of this, the companion app [b]may cause a security warning[/b] on Windows  and/or some anti-virus software. We assure you this companion app is completely safe, and you can allow it access to the system's network. There are currently no plans or means to support [u]Bluetooth[/u] heart rate devices on Windows 7.

[*][b][u]Note: Windows 32-bit[/u][/b] 
Nevermind does [u][i]not[/i][/u] [i]officially[/i] support Windows 32-bit machines. That said, we do try to ensure that the experience can run on 32-bit machines. If any [b]Windows 32-bit[/b] players experience any instability after this update, please let us know. You can always email us at support@nevermindgame.com
[/list]

notes.title: Apple Watch Support & Update on Upcoming NEW Levels
notes.content:
Hi Everyone! 

We have one piece of exciting news and an update on our upcoming new Nevermind levels (which will be made available as part of a free update)! 

[h1]Apple Watch Support![/h1] 
At long last, Nevermind now supports Apple Watch on all currently available platforms - including Mac and Windows!

To use the Apple Watch as a sensor, all you need to do is: 
[olist]
[*] Download the [b][url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/id1077209743]iPhone Nevermind Companion App[/url][/b]  
( https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/id1077209743 )
IMPORTANT: As with all Apple Watch apps, an iPhone 5 or later is required.  
[*] Make sure that the Apple Watch app installs alongside it. You may need to go into “Watch” app on your phone to ensure that it has permission to install to your watch.
[*] Launch the app from your phone.  Make sure to enable it read Heart Rate data when it asks.
[*] Open up the app on the Watch (if it didn’t open automatically). 
[*] Give the Watch app a few moments to start reading your heart rate. You should see it update on the phone shortly thereafter. 
[*] Launch Nevermind from your Mac or Windows machine.

The heart rate sensors, on the other hand, pick up indications of [i]physiological[/i] reactions. notes.title: Version: 1.01.57 (update to installer only)
notes.content:
[h1]Build Notes for Version 1.01.57 - Installer Update[/h1]

[b][u]NOTE: No Sensor is Required.[/u][/b]
You do [b]NOT [/b] need a biofeedback sensor to play [i]Nevermind.[/i] Without a sensor, the biofeedback-specific features will be unavailable, but the core game itself will be fully playable.

[b][u]Updates:[/u][/b]
[list]

[*][b][u]Bug Fix:[/u] Trojan Horse False Positive Fix[/b] 
We have updated the installer (no edits to the game itself have been made for this update) in order to resolve the issue some players were experiencing in which Windows Defender (or another virus scanning program) would flag Nevermind as a trojan horse. We are confident that our sensor code was just being mis-identified as a trojan horse and that the warning was a false positive. And, just to be [i]extra[/i] safe, we have quadruple-checked to make sure that Nevermind contains no viruses or trojan horses or anything nasty of that nature. 

Note: If any [b]Windows 32-bit[/b] players experience any instability after this update, please let us know ( you can always email us at support@nevermindgame.com ). 

If [i]anyone[/i] has any questions about this update or further concerns about the false positive warning, please feel free to email us at support@nevermindgame.com at any time. 
[/list]

[list]

[*][b][u]Flying Mollusk Logo Screen:[/u][/b] 
The Flying Mollusk logo screen may occasionally linger a little longer than it had before. This rare occurrence has to do with some under the hood stuff that happens at that point in time.  While some players may experience this shortly after updating the game, we’ve found that it only happens once and should return to its normal duration afterwards. 

[*][b][u]DirectX 9:[/u][/b]

This companion application is opened and closed by the game, and can be found as a taskbar icon next to the clock during play. This companion application uses network protocols to communicate with [i]Nevermind[/i]. Because of this, the companion app [b]may cause a security warning[/b] on Windows  and/or some anti-virus software. We assure you this companion app is completely safe, and you can allow it access to the system's network. There are currently no plans or means to support [u]Bluetooth[/u] heart rate devices on Windows 7.

[*][b][u]Fear UI:[/u][/b] 
To see an [b]on-screen indicator of your “fear level,”[/b] go into the Options menu and select “Fear UI On.” (Note: option only appears if playing with a supported biofeedback sensor).

[*][b][u]First Person Control Familiarity:[/u][/b] 
[i]Nevermind[/i] uses standard “first person” controls (WASD/arrows and mouse). Familiarity with this control scheme is recommended. 
[/list]

notes.title: Updates on Nevermind’s Launch Timeline
notes.content:
[h1]We’re excited to announce that the full version of Nevermind will be launching on Steam [b]later this month![/b][/h1] 
More details will be announced in the coming weeks.

[h1] Windows[/h1] 
Nevermind will continue to fully support Win 8.1 and we’re currently working on bringing Nevermind to Win 10. This version will be available at some point after the launch this month. Nevermind is [i]unofficially[/i] supported on Win 7. This means that it generally [i]should[/i] work just fine on Win 7, but there may be a few platform-specific bugs here and there that haven’t been caught. If you find any, let us know either via the [url=steamcommunity.com/app/342260/discussions/2/] Discussions forums[/url]   or directly via email at support@nevermindgame.com. 


[h1] Oculus Rift[/h1] 
The Oculus Rift version of Nevermind will be available when the Oculus Rift itself will be available to everyone ([url=www.oculus.com/en-us/blog/first-look-at-the-rift-shipping-q1-2016/]which will be Q1 of 2016[/url]). We’ll be using the extra time to continue the development and optimization of the Rift version of Nevermind to ensure it’s the best experience it can be in virtual reality.


[h1] Additional Sensors[/h1] 
We will not be slowing down our R&D efforts to expand Nevermind’s [url=http://www.nevermindgame.com/sensors/]list of supported sensors[/url] post-launch. We have some exciting things in the works and, as new sensors become available, we’ll be sure to announce them here. 


[h1] New Content[/h1] 
Our vision for Nevermind is to continue to create new levels and content after launch and release those new levels on something akin to an episodic basis. Much will, of course, depend on how launch does, but all of the amazing support and feedback we’ve received throughout Early Access has us feeling pretty optimistic. 

Thank you for your continued support and here's to an exciting September!

[list]

[*][b][u]Bug alert: Neuromapping[/u][/b] - We have found that some users are unable to trigger Neuromapping functionality. We are looking into the issue and will post an update as soon as it is fixed.
